einzeiler: Inside Internal Affairs with a veteran cop on discipline, corruption, and the thin blue…
kurzfassung: Former LAPD sergeant and internal affairs investigator Marlon Marrache discusses the realities of police accountability, officer representation, and departmental discipline. He shares insights from his 24-year career, examining why cops fear internal affairs and how internal investigations are conducted. The conversation also covers the evolution of street policing from the 1990s to the era of body cameras.
stichpunkte: Marlon Marrache served 24 years in the LAPD, working both as an officer on the road and later in internal affairs and the officer representation section.
Internal affairs departments face a heavy negative stigma within law enforcement, often viewed by street cops as the "rat squad."
Most public complaints against police officers are adjudicated as unfounded, highlighting the rarity of sustained disciplinary issues.
The process of internal investigations often focuses heavily on off-duty behavior and truthfulness during compelled interviews.
Body-worn cameras have fundamentally changed policing by providing greater transparency and accountability for both officers and the public.
Marrache transitioned into consulting and media after retirement, using his platform to discuss police culture and bridge gaps between law enforcement and the community.

beschreibung:
What really happens inside police Internal Affairs and can the system itself get it wrong?
In Episode 126 of The Wild Chaos Podcast, Bam sits down with retired LAPD Sergeant Marlon Marrache, a 24-year law enforcement veteran who experienced police discipline from both sides: first representing officers accused of misconduct, and later working inside Internal Affairs. Both sides of the fence.
Watch the full episode here: https://youtu.be/6r-psAzvW-g
This isn't a surface level conversation about police policy.
Bam puts Marlon directly in the hot seat with questions submitted by cops themselves.
Can Internal Affairs be weaponized?
Do innocent officers get found guilty?
Can politically connected officers receive different treatment? Do cases ever simply disappear?
Who investigates Internal Affairs when Internal Affairs gets it wrong?
Marlon breaks down misconduct investigations, false and misleading statements, officer-involved shootings, compelled interviews, administrative hearings, police discipline, departmental politics, and the mistakes that can destroy an officer's career.
He also explains why something seemingly minor can become career-ending when an officer isn't truthful during an Internal Affairs investigation—and why he believes departments need better checks and balances.
But near the end of the conversation, the badge disappears. And when asked what he ultimately wants the world to remember about him, it isn't LAPD, Internal Affairs, rank or career. It's being a great dad.
This episode is about accountability inside law enforcement—but it's also about identity, family, purpose and what remains when the career finally ends.
